```{r}
# Clear the workspace so the script starts from a clean state
rm(list = ls())
```

**Load required packages**

```{r}
# Configure R packages
# pacman streamlines package management: it installs missing packages and attaches them in one call
if (!require(pacman)){
        install.packages("pacman")  # install pacman itself if not yet available
        library(pacman)             # attach it
}

# Load all packages used in the cleaning pipeline
pacman::p_load(
  "tidyverse", "ggplot2", "cowplot", "bruceR","ggstatsplot", "papaja",
  "palmerpenguins", "dplyr", "patchwork", "RColorBrewer","reader"
)

# Source the custom raincloud-plot helper functions (used for later visualization)
# source("Functions/R_rainclouds.R")
```

## 1. Read data

**Step 1: Read raw data files under target directory**

```{r}
# Set the path of the folder holding the raw experimental data
parent_folder <- "../../3_Data/RawData/"

# Create an empty vector to store all file paths
file_list <- c()

# List every raw per-participant file (names like "exp3_subj_7.csv")
file_list <- list.files(
    path = parent_folder,
    pattern = "*exp3_subj.*\\.csv$",  # regex: contains "exp3_subj." and ends with ".csv"
    full.names = TRUE                 # return full paths rather than bare filenames
  )

# Create an empty list to store the loaded datasets
df_list_1 <- list()

# Read each file and store it in the list (the filename without extension is the element name)
for (file in file_list) {
  # Get the filename without path and without the .csv extension
  file_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
  # tryCatch keeps the loop running even if a single file fails to load
  tryCatch({
    df_list_1[[file_name]] <- read.csv(file)
  })
}

# Report how many files were loaded and their names
cat("Total loaded files:", length(df_list_1), "\n")
print(names(df_list_1))
```
## 2. Data cleaning

**Step 2: Clean each participant's data**

```{r}
# Create the output folder if it does not already exist
output_path <- "../../3_Data/CleanData"
if (!dir.exists(output_path)) {
  dir.create(output_path, recursive = TRUE)  # recursive = also create missing parent folders
}

# Clean each participant's raw dataset in a loop
for (file_name in names(df_list_1)) {
  data <- df_list_1[[file_name]]   # the current participant's raw data

  # Extract the demographic info from the survey part (collected at the start of the experiment)
  participant_info <- data[data$part == "survey", "response"]
  # Strip braces and quotes so only plain "key:value" pairs remain
  participant_info <- gsub("[{}\"]", "", participant_info)
  # Split the string on commas into individual "key:value" entries
  info_list <- strsplit(participant_info, ",")[[1]]

  # Create an empty dataframe that will hold this participant's metadata
  participant_data <- data.frame(
    subj_idx = file_name,          # placeholder; replaced with a numeric ID below
    Sex = as.character(NA),
    Age = as.numeric(NA),
    Handedness = as.character(NA),
    Color_blindness = as.character(NA),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Split the filename (e.g. "exp3_subj_7") by underscore
  split_data <- strsplit(participant_data$subj_idx, "_")
  # Keep only the digits of the last element (e.g. "7") and convert to a numeric participant ID
  participant_data$subj_idx <- as.numeric(lapply(split_data, function(x) {
    gsub("[^0-9]", "", x[[3]])   # strip all non-digit characters
  }))

  # Loop over the "key:value" pairs and fill the metadata dataframe
  for (info in info_list) {
    key_value <- strsplit(info, ":")[[1]]   # split each entry on the colon
    key <- trimws(key_value[1])             # trim whitespace from the key
    value <- trimws(key_value[2])           # trim whitespace from the value
    if (key == "sex"){
      # Recode the Chinese sex labels into numeric codes: male = 1, female = 2
      participant_data$Sex <- switch(
        value, "男" = 1, "女" = 2
      )
    }
    if (key == "age") participant_data$Age <- as.numeric(value)              # store age as a number
    if (key == "hands") participant_data$Handedness <- value                 # store handedness as text
    if (key == "color_blindness") participant_data$Color_blindness <- value  # store color-blindness self-report
  }

  # Extract the behavioral trials of the three choice tasks
  behavior_data <- data[
    data$part %in% c("RDK_overlap","RDK_color","RDK_shape"),  # keep only choice-task rows
    c(
      "part", "rt", "response", "correct", "dot_color","dot_shape",
      "association"                                            # columns needed downstream
    )
  ]

  # Extract the formal trials of each task
  official_trials <- do.call(
  rbind,   # row-bind the per-task results into a single dataframe
  lapply(unique(behavior_data$part), function(part) {
    part_data <- behavior_data[behavior_data$part == part, ]  # trials of one task
    if (part %in% c("RDK_overlap", "RDK_color", "RDK_shape")) {
      return(tail(part_data, 128))   # the formal trials
    } else {
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
)

  # Column-bind the participant metadata with the cleaned behavioral trials
  final_data <- cbind(participant_data, official_trials)

  # Export the cleaned per-participant dataset to CSV
  output_file <- file.path(output_path, paste0(file_name, "_Clean.csv"))
  write.csv(final_data, output_file, row.names = FALSE)  # no extra row-index column
}
```

**Read cleaned datasets**
**Load all cleaned files and stack them into one trial-level dataframe**

```{r message=FALSE}
# Set the path of the folder holding the cleaned per-participant files
folder_path <- "../../3_Data/CleanData"

# List all cleaned CSV files matching the pattern "*exp3_subj_*.csv"
file_list <- list.files(
  path = folder_path,
  pattern = "*exp3_subj_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE
)

# Create an empty list to store the cleaned datasets
df_list_1 <- list()

# Read every cleaned file and stack them into a single dataframe
for (file in file_list) {
  file_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))  # filename without path/extension
  # Read with explicit column types: "correct" as logical, everything else guessed automatically
  df <- read_csv(file, col_types = cols(
    correct = col_logical(),
    .default = col_guess()
  ))
  df_list_1[[file_name]] <- df   # store the dataset under its filename
}
# Vertically stack all per-participant datasets into one trial-level dataframe
data <- dplyr::bind_rows(df_list_1)

# Remove intermediate objects to keep the workspace tidy
rm(participant_info, info_list, participant_data, split_data,
   behavior_data, official_trials, final_data, output_file, file, file_list,
   file_name, folder_path, info, key, key_value, value)
```

## 3. Demographic summary statistics

```{r}
# Build a demographic summary table from the cleaned data
df.basic <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(subj_idx, Age, Sex) %>%              # keep only ID, age, and sex columns
  dplyr::distinct(subj_idx, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%    # one row per participant
  dplyr::mutate(
    subj_group = dplyr::case_when(                   # label participants by subject-number range
      subj_idx >= 1 & subj_idx <= 40 ~ "Group1 (motion)",
      subj_idx >= 40 & subj_idx <= 80 ~ "Group2 (color)",
    )
  ) %>%
  # dplyr::group_by(subj_group) %>%                  # (commented out: summary is computed over all participants)
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = length(subj_idx),                            # total number of participants
    Nf = length(Sex[Sex == "2"]),                    # number of women (coded 2)
    Nm = length(Sex[Sex == "1"]),                    # number of men (coded 1)
    Age_mean = round(mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 2),    # mean age (NAs excluded, rounded to 2 decimals)
    Age_sd = round(sd(Age, na.rm = TRUE), 2),        # standard deviation of age
    .groups = "drop"
  )

df.basic   # print the demographic summary
```
## 4. Further data preprocessing

**Define functions to compute mean RT, accuracy, and self‑other difference (SPE)**

```{r}
# Compute mean RT (correct trials only) and accuracy per participant x task x association
compute_rt_acc <- function(data){
  data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(part %in% c("RDK_overlap","RDK_color","RDK_shape")) %>%  # keep only formal choice-task trials
    dplyr::filter(rt != -1) %>%                 # drop trials with missing RTs (coded as -1)
    dplyr::group_by(subj_idx, part, association) %>%  # aggregate within each condition cell
    dplyr::summarise(
      # rt = mean(rt, na.rm = TRUE),             # (alternative: mean over all trials)
      rt = mean(rt[correct == 1], na.rm = TRUE), # mean RT over correct trials only
      acc = sum(correct == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / n()  # proportion of correct responses
    )

  return(data)
}

# Compute the self-other difference (the SPE effect size) per participant and task
compute_diff <- function(data, keepMatch=FALSE){
  group_vars <- if(keepMatch) {
    c("subj_idx", "part")   # grouping variables used when keepMatch = TRUE
  } else {
    c("subj_idx", "part")   # (both branches are identical here)
  }

  data_agg <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(part %in% c("RDK_overlap","RDK_color","RDK_shape")) %>%  # formal tasks only
    dplyr::group_by_at(group_vars) %>%   # group by the chosen grouping variables
    dplyr::summarise(
      # Widen the data: separate columns for the self and other conditions
      rt_other = mean(rt[association == "other"], na.rm = TRUE),
      rt_self = mean(rt[association == "self"], na.rm = TRUE),
      acc_other = mean(acc[association == "other"], na.rm = TRUE),
      acc_self = mean(acc[association == "self"], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Calculate difference scores per participant and task
  data_result <- data_agg %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      rt_diff_os = rt_other - rt_self,   # positive value = self advantage (faster for self)
      acc_diff_so = acc_self - acc_other # positive value = self advantage (higher accuracy for self)
    )

  return(data_result)
}
```

**Step 3: Extract shape‑group and color‑group datasets separately**

```{r}
# Trial-level cleaning: keep only trials with plausible RTs (100-3000 ms, non-missing)
data <- data %>%
  dplyr::filter(rt >= 100 & rt <= 3000, !is.na(rt))

# ---- Shape-associated group (participants 1-40) ----
data1 <- data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    subj_idx %in% c( seq(1, 40))) %>%   # select participants of the shape group
  dplyr::mutate(correct = as.numeric(as.logical(correct))) %>%  # recode logical to 0/1
  dplyr::group_by(subj_idx, part) %>%        # group by participant and task
  dplyr::mutate(subj_acc = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # overall accuracy per participant/task
  dplyr::ungroup()


# Long-format trial-level dataset for the shape group
data_shape <- data1 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    subj_idx, rt, correct, part, response, association, dot_color, dot_shape  # columns needed downstream
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(correct = as.numeric(as.logical(correct))) %>%  # ensure 0/1 numeric coding
  dplyr::mutate(rt = rt / 1000) %>%    # convert RT from milliseconds to seconds
  dplyr::mutate(group = "shape")       # tag the dimension associated with identity

# (commented out) alternative export of the shape-group dataset
# output_file <- base::file.path(output_path, "data_motion.csv")
# utils::write.csv(data_motion, output_file, row.names = FALSE)


# Mean RT/accuracy per participant x task x association for the shape group
data_shape_rt_acc <- compute_rt_acc(data1) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = "shape")


# Self-other difference scores for the shape group
data_shape_diff <- compute_diff(data_shape_rt_acc) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subj_idx = as.factor(subj_idx))  # store the participant ID as a factor

# ---- Color-associated group (participants 41-80) ----
data2 <- data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    subj_idx %in% c( seq(41, 80))) %>%   # select participants of the color group
  dplyr::mutate(correct = as.numeric(as.logical(correct))) %>%  # recode logical to 0/1
  dplyr::group_by(subj_idx, part) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subj_acc = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # overall accuracy per participant/task
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Long-format trial-level dataset for the color group
data_color <- data2 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    subj_idx, rt, correct, part, response, association, dot_color, dot_shape
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(correct = as.numeric(as.logical(correct))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rt = rt / 1000) %>%    # convert RT from milliseconds to seconds
  dplyr::mutate(group = "color")       # tag the dimension associated with identity


# Mean RT/accuracy per participant x task x association for the color group
data_color_rt_acc <- compute_rt_acc(data2) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = "color")


# Self-other difference scores for the color group
# (the second call recomputes and overwrites the first one)
data_color_diff <- compute_diff(data_color_rt_acc) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subj_idx = as.factor(subj_idx))

data_color_diff <- compute_diff(data_color_rt_acc) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(subj_idx = as.factor(subj_idx))
```


**Step 4: Merge and save final datasets**

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Step 5: Recode task_type and save the final datasets
# Map each group x task combination onto relevant / irrelevant / overlap and export data_sbfa.csv and data_all.csv.
# ============================================================

# Build the aggregated dataset for the sequential Bayes factor analysis (SBFA)
data_sbfa <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_color_rt_acc, data_shape_rt_acc) %>%  # stack both groups vertically
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Derive the task type from the group (associated dimension) and the task (part):
    #  - judging the associated dimension  -> identity-relevant task
    #  - judging the other dimension       -> identity-irrelevant task
    #  - RDK_overlap is the identity-choice task
    task_type = case_when(
      # Rules for the color-associated group
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "relevant",
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "irrelevant",
      # Rules for the shape-associated group
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "irrelevant",
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "relevant",
      # identity-choice task
      part == "RDK_overlap" ~ "overlap",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_               # fallback: anything else is undefined
    )
  )

# Save the SBFA dataset
output_file <- base::file.path(output_path, "data_sbfa.csv")
utils::write.csv(data_sbfa, output_file, row.names = FALSE)

# Build the trial-level dataset for the main analyses (BHM and HDDM)
data_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(data_color, data_shape) %>%  # stack the two group datasets vertically
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Same task-type recoding as above, applied at the trial level
    task_type = case_when(
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "relevant",
      group == "color" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "irrelevant",
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_color" ~ "irrelevant",
      group == "shape" & part == "RDK_shape" ~ "relevant",
      part == "RDK_overlap" ~ "overlap",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Save the main trial-level dataset
output_file <- base::file.path(output_path, "data_all.csv")
utils::write.csv(data_all, output_file, row.names = FALSE)
```
